title: Things I can do
subject: Careers

thread_tags.line: Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
thread_tags.rationale: S: reflect on skills or choices. So: listen and share task talk. IL: choose a response mode and task route. MR: value different skills and roles without ranking people.

label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Identify one strength and link it to a work task.
display_objective: Identify one strength and link it to a work task.
approved_activity: Match fictional worker cards to strengths such as checking, sorting or helping.

calendar_note: Year A. 2–6 November 2026. One 40-minute lesson. No day or clock slot inferred. Week 7 is assessing.
where_this_leads: This helps me see how a skill can be useful at work.

accreditation: The qualification and the accredited unit: any mapping is for staff to confirm from the actual evidence. No criteria or completion are inferred.
assessment: Weeks 1–6 are formative. Week 7 is the assessing lesson. Keep actual responses, support, gaps and next steps in the evidence record.

routes.Supported: Supported: choose from two skill cards, then sort three tokens with a model available.

vocab.definition: Look to see if it is right.
Give a hand with a task.

cases.text: A worker puts tins in neat rows.
cases.judgement: Sort: the action puts items in order.
cases.next_step: Ask what the worker does that shows sorting.

cases.text: A worker checks boxes on a list.
cases.judgement: Check: the worker compares items with a list.
cases.next_step: Ask the learner to point to the action or read it back.

cases.text: A worker shows a new worker where pots go.
cases.judgement: Help: the worker gives another person useful information.
cases.next_step: Accept pointing or a short phrase; do not require fluent speech.

cases.text: A worker puts like shapes in sets.
cases.judgement: Sort: the worker groups the same shapes.
cases.next_step: Link to the classroom token task.

cases.text: A worker spots a card in the wrong set.
cases.judgement: Check: the worker notices a mismatch.
cases.next_step: Ask what could be changed; keep the initial sort recorded.

cases.text: A worker gets a tray for a team mate.
cases.judgement: Help: the worker supports another person’s task.
cases.next_step: Accept another relevant skill with a reason grounded in the card.

Owner-approved standalone Careers outline, 26 October 2026. The combined workbook strand supplies context; it does not replace this approved weekly objective.
How can a skill help with a job?

CAREERS-BUILD-A2-W01-E1: A strength-to-task match and an individual observation of the practical task, including support used.

For each learner, print both evidence pages and the support pack. Cut six shape tokens and the three skill labels from page 3; keep the two sorting mats intact. Provide a clear tray and large paper tokens only. Read the worker cards aloud if needed. Prepare one duplicate set for modelling. Use 3–4 learners, with individual evidence and an adult or solo route available.
Year A. Autumn 2 Week 1: 2–6 November 2026. One 40-minute Careers lesson. No day or clock slot is inferred. This lesson is formative. Week 7 is the assessing lesson.
This helps me see how a skill can be useful at work.
Open the title before the timed sequence.
Read the objective and success checks.
Individual task with the chosen route.
Record actual work, response and support.
Individual exit response and next step.

A: checking is supported by the stated action. Speed, neatness or confidence alone is not the target. Recheck using the helper card: ask which action shows helping. Accept another skill only when the learner links it to a stated action.

Supported: choose from two skill cards, then sort three tokens with a model available. Independent: match three worker cards, sort six tokens and check both sets. Aspire: explain a second skill, or show how checking improves the first sort.

Use four minutes to match worker cards to sort, check or help. Use five minutes for an individual shape sort: supported route uses three tokens; independent route uses all six. Use three minutes to check sets and identify one skill actually shown. Give one specific prompt and preserve the first result and changed response. A card match alone does not prove the practical skill.
Read aloud, point, scribe exact words or use the usual communication aid. Record support without treating speech speed or handwriting as the target.

All worker profiles, job roles, employers and settings are fictional. Use only the supplied classroom tasks; no real employers, applications or personal contact details. No names are required. Do not ask about family, body or private experiences. Respect a choice to pause or respond privately. No forced pair work or public performance. Follow the setting’s safeguarding route if a concern is raised.

Record the selected worker card and skill, then the number and pattern of tokens sorted and checked. Note exact prompts and what the learner did. Ask for one skill demonstrated in this task, without asking for private experiences. A pupil may identify a skill to develop rather than claim it as a fixed strength. This is formative evidence for Week 7.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // self-edit · ? read back · R responded · E evidence in the evidence record. R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner response in their own colour. E is recorded only when actual evidence is banked. Record support and unfinished work; blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Space: calm seating and clear resources. Voice: choose a mode, reason or help request. Audience: an adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next step changed in response.
S: reflect on skills or choices. So: listen and share task talk. IL: choose a response mode and task route. MR: value different skills and roles without ranking people.

Offer an authentic explanation, choice or help request to the Communication portfolio. The receiving teacher decides how actual work fits the evidence record; no qualification criterion is assigned here.

These are teaching guides. Record the learner’s actual response and support. The fictional worker cards do not describe real people, employers or vacancies.

This made-up worker sorts tins. The tins go in neat rows. Sorting is a useful skill. Now watch me sort these cards. I put like shapes in a set. I check each set to make sure.

A: checking is supported by the stated action. Speed, neatness or confidence alone is not the target. Recheck using the helper card: ask which action shows helping. Accept another skill only when the learner links it to a stated action.

Record the selected worker card and skill, then the number and pattern of tokens sorted and checked. Note exact prompts and what the learner did. Ask for one skill demonstrated in this task, without asking for private experiences. A pupil may identify a skill to develop rather than claim it as a fixed strength. This is formative evidence for Week 7.

The token sheet has three circles and three squares. A correct full sort has three circles on the circle mat and three squares on the square mat. For the Supported route, give any three tokens and record the actual set. Record the first sort before any prompt; then note the changed result. A pupil may point to sort, check or help if the observed action supports it.
A strength is not a ranking of people. A skill can grow with practice. Sorting, checking and helping can all matter in many jobs. The worker’s appearance does not tell us their skill.

All worker profiles, job roles, employers and settings are fictional. Use only the supplied classroom tasks; no real employers, applications or personal contact details. No names are required. Do not ask about family, body or private experiences. Respect a choice to pause or respond privately. No forced pair work or public performance. Follow the setting’s safeguarding route if a concern is raised.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // self-edit · ? read back · R responded · E evidence in the evidence record. R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner response in their own colour. E is recorded only when actual evidence is banked. Record support and unfinished work; blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
If work is incomplete, name the gap and arrange a supported follow-up. No qualification completion is claimed.
